description: An introduction to how chemical elements are arranged in the periodic table by atomic number into periods and groups, and the general properties and trends of metals, non-metals, metalloids and selected groups.

mcq.questionText: In the modern periodic table, elements are arranged in order of increasing what?
mcq.explanation: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (number of protons).

mcq.questionText: What name is given to the horizontal rows of the periodic table?
mcq.explanation: The horizontal rows in the periodic table are called periods, while the vertical columns are called groups.

mcq.questionText: What name is given to the vertical columns of the periodic table?
mcq.explanation: Vertical columns are called groups; elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.

mcq.questionText: Elements found in the same group of the periodic table have the same number of what?
mcq.explanation: Members of the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which is why they show similar chemical behaviour.

mcq.questionText: The number of occupied energy levels (shells) of an element is shown by its what?
mcq.explanation: The period number tells you how many electron shells (energy levels) an atom of that element has.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a property typical of metals?

options.text: Good conductors of heat and electricity
Exist mostly as gases at room temperature

mcq.explanation: Metals are generally shiny, malleable and good conductors of heat and electricity.

mcq.questionText: Elements that have properties of both metals and non-metals are called?
mcq.explanation: Metalloids, such as silicon and boron, show some properties of metals and some of non-metals.

mcq.questionText: Which group of the periodic table contains the alkali metals?
mcq.explanation: Group I elements (lithium, sodium, potassium, etc.) are called the alkali metals.

mcq.questionText: The elements of Group VII are commonly known as the?
mcq.explanation: Group VII elements such as fluorine, chlorine and bromine are called the halogens.

mcq.questionText: Which group contains very unreactive gases such as helium, neon and argon?
mcq.explanation: Group 0 (also called Group VIII) contains the noble gases, which are very unreactive because their outer shells are full.

mcq.questionText: An element with electron arrangement 2,8,1 belongs to which group and period?
mcq.explanation: It has 1 valence electron (Group I) and 3 occupied shells (Period 3); this element is sodium.

mcq.questionText: As you move down Group I from lithium to potassium, the reactivity of the metals generally?
mcq.explanation: Reactivity of alkali metals increases down the group because the outer electron is more easily lost.

mcq.questionText: At room temperature, the halogen chlorine exists as a?
mcq.explanation: Chlorine is a greenish-yellow poisonous gas at room temperature.

mcq.questionText: An element in Group II of the periodic table has a valency of?
mcq.explanation: Group II elements have 2 valence electrons, so their combining power (valency) is 2.

mcq.questionText: Which scientist is credited with arranging the elements by atomic mass and leaving gaps for undiscovered elements?
mcq.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic mass and left gaps for elements not yet discovered.

fib.questionText: In the periodic table, the vertical columns are called _____.
fib.explanation: Vertical columns are groups; elements in the same group have similar properties.

fib.questionText: The horizontal rows of the periodic table are called _____.
fib.explanation: Horizontal rows are called periods and show the number of electron shells.

fib.questionText: Modern elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic _____.
fib.explanation: Atomic number (the number of protons) is the basis of arrangement in the modern periodic table.

fib.questionText: Elements of Group I are collectively known as the alkali _____.
fib.explanation: Group I elements are soft, reactive metals known as alkali metals.

fib.questionText: Elements of Group VII are collectively called the _____.
fib.explanation: The halogens are reactive non-metals found in Group VII.

fib.questionText: Elements showing properties of both metals and non-metals are called _____.
fib.explanation: Metalloids such as silicon lie along the dividing line between metals and non-metals.

fib.questionText: The very unreactive gases in Group 0 are called the _____ gases.
fib.explanation: Noble gases are unreactive because they have full outer electron shells.

fib.questionText: The number of valence electrons of an element is equal to its _____ number (for groups I to VII).
fib.explanation: For main-group elements the group number equals the number of outer electrons.

fib.questionText: Going down Group I, the reactivity of the metals _____.
fib.explanation: Reactivity increases down Group I as the outer electron is lost more easily.

fib.questionText: An atom with electron arrangement 2,8,7 has a valency of _____.
fib.explanation: With 7 outer electrons it needs to gain 1 electron, giving a valency of 1 (this element is chlorine).

tf.questionText: Elements in the modern periodic table are arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.
tf.explanation: They are arranged by increasing atomic number, not atomic mass.

tf.questionText: Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons.
tf.explanation: Having the same number of outer electrons gives group members similar chemical properties.

tf.questionText: The period number of an element tells you the number of occupied electron shells.
tf.explanation: The period number equals the number of energy levels (shells) in the atom.

tf.questionText: Metals are generally poor conductors of electricity.
tf.explanation: Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity.

tf.questionText: Noble gases are very reactive because they have one electron in their outer shell.
tf.explanation: Noble gases are unreactive because their outer shells are full (stable).

tf.questionText: Halogens are reactive non-metals found in Group VII.
tf.explanation: Group VII halogens, such as chlorine and bromine, are reactive non-metals.

tf.questionText: Alkali metals are stored under oil because they react with water and air.
tf.explanation: Alkali metals are very reactive, so they are kept under oil to keep out water and air.

tf.questionText: Silicon is an example of a metalloid.
tf.explanation: Silicon shows properties of both metals and non-metals, so it is a metalloid.

tf.questionText: Non-metals are generally found on the left-hand side of the periodic table.
tf.explanation: Non-metals are mostly on the right-hand side; metals are on the left.

tf.questionText: The reactivity of halogens increases as you go down Group VII.
tf.explanation: Halogen reactivity decreases down the group because gaining an electron becomes harder.

summary.questionText: Basis of arrangement of the modern periodic table
summary.correctAnswer: Elements are arranged by increasing atomic number.
summary.explanation: Atomic number equals the number of protons in the atom.
The period number shows the number of electron shells.

summary.correctAnswer: Groups are the vertical columns of elements with similar properties.
summary.explanation: Group members share the same number of valence electrons.

summary.correctAnswer: Metals are shiny, malleable and good conductors of heat and electricity.
summary.explanation: They are found mainly on the left side of the table.

summary.correctAnswer: Non-metals are usually dull, brittle and poor conductors.
summary.explanation: They are found mainly on the right side of the table.

summary.correctAnswer: Metalloids have properties of both metals and non-metals.
Soft, very reactive metals with one valence electron.
summary.explanation: Examples are lithium, sodium and potassium.

summary.correctAnswer: Reactive non-metals with seven valence electrons.
summary.explanation: Examples are fluorine, chlorine and bromine.

summary.correctAnswer: Unreactive gases with full outer electron shells.
summary.explanation: Examples are helium, neon and argon.

summary.correctAnswer: Valency can be worked out from the number of valence electrons (group number).
summary.explanation: For example, Group I has valency 1 and Group II has valency 2.

hoq.questionText: An element X has the electron arrangement 2,8,2. To which group and period does X belong, and what is its likely valency?
hoq.explanation: It has 2 outer electrons (Group II) and 3 shells (Period 3), giving a valency of 2; this element is magnesium.

hoq.questionText: Two elements P and Q have atomic numbers 11 and 17 respectively. Which statement is correct about them?

options.text: Both are noble gases in the same group
P is a reactive metal and Q is a reactive non-metal, both in Period 3
P and Q are both in Group I
Q is a metal and P is a non-metal

hoq.explanation: P (2,8,1) is sodium, a Group I reactive metal; Q (2,8,7) is chlorine, a Group VII reactive non-metal; both lie in Period 3.

hoq.questionText: Why does the reactivity of alkali metals increase down Group I while that of the halogens decreases down Group VII?

options.text: Both groups gain electrons more easily down the group
Alkali metals lose their outer electron more easily down the group, while halogens find it harder to gain an electron down the group
Atomic size stays constant in both groups
Both groups lose electrons more easily down the group

hoq.explanation: Going down a group, atoms get larger; the outer electron is held less tightly, so metals lose it more easily, but halogens attract an extra electron less strongly.
